steps.what: Negotiate with government leaders and utility companies
Meet businesses and special interest representatives
Gain support for projects and eliminate potential obstacles

tasks.design: The manager negotiates with government leaders, businesses, special interest representatives, and utility companies to gain support for new projects and to eliminate potential obstacles. Nothing is sent by {EMAIL}. The negotiations stay at full effort.
tasks.previous_blocker: The manager meets the people and works through the obstacles.
tasks.enabler_now: No stored brief replaces the negotiation.
tasks.still_hard: Gaining support and judging an obstacle stay with the manager.
tasks.human_edge: The manager does not claim support that the other party has not given.
tasks.altitude: The negotiation stays the work. Nothing in it is shortened.

reach.task: Say what would block the project
reach.learn: Which obstacles that office can remove.

evidence.claim: Negotiating support for a project with leaders, businesses, and utility companies stays manual.

assumptions: The work starts with a project that needs support and ends when the manager has negotiated or stopped.
No new record is required. Upkeep is zero.
A permit application, if one follows, is a different task.
unknowns: Which offices must be heard before the project can proceed.
research_questions: Which obstacles remained after the last round of talks?

already_counted.description: Negotiating with government leaders and utility companies is already in the manager's step.

incremental.description: No new upkeep: the negotiations add no record.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: every talk is still held by the manager. High: the same negotiations remain, with no step removed. No upkeep is added, so the low does not go below zero. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyze whether a property should be acquired

steps.what: Show stored information on property values, taxes, zoning, and traffic volume
Analyze population growth and traffic patterns
Determine if properties should be acquired

tasks.design: The manager analyzes information on property values, taxes, zoning, population growth, and traffic volume and patterns to determine if properties should be acquired. {DOCS} shows stored figures. A blank figure stays blank and is not treated as zero. The analysis and the decision stay at full effort.
tasks.previous_blocker: The manager gathered the figures and decided.
tasks.enabler_now: Figures already stored can be shown together.
tasks.still_hard: Analyzing what the figures mean, and deciding to acquire, stay with the manager.
tasks.human_edge: The manager does not recommend an acquisition when a value or a tax figure is blank.
tasks.altitude: The decision stays the manager's. The screen only shows stored figures.

reach.task: Decide whether to make an offer
reach.learn: Which properties the owner will not buy.

evidence.claim: Stored values, taxes, zoning, and traffic figures can be shown together. Deciding to acquire stays manual.

assumptions: The work starts with a property that might be acquired and ends when the manager has determined whether it should be, or stops.
A figure row has property identifier, figure type, period, and value, entered by the manager from a published source or a survey. A blank value is left blank.
Showing the figures does not shorten the analysis or the decision. No offer is sent in this task.
unknowns: Which year's traffic and population figures the owner wants used.
research_questions: How often was a value or a tax figure blank, so the manager stopped?

already_counted.description: Deciding whether properties should be acquired is already in the manager's step.

incremental.description: Correct a tax or traffic figure the manager finds is for the wrong year.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: figures are often blank, so the analysis is unchanged. High: the figures show, and the manager still analyzes and decides. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The manager still inspects sites, meets people, and decides rents, eligibility, and staff matters. A payment, contract, purchase, advertisement, or record is sent or written only after the manager accepts that version.
reach: An owner receives only a budget or a payment list the manager has accepted.
A contractor receives only a bid request or a contract the manager has accepted.
skills_to_grow: Stop when an amount, a date, or a required document is blank.
Accept or refuse the exact version before a send or a write.
Keep site inspections, tenant conversations, and eligibility decisions in their own hands.
role.ambitious_version: Every property has a budget and a record the owner can trust, and the manager still decides the exception.

job.title: Property, Real Estate, and Community Association Managers
